source.title: Cross-Lingual Representation Alignment by Token-Level Optimal Transport in a Language-Agnostic Space
source.authors: Taisei Yamamoto; Ryoma Kumon; Danushka Bollegala; Hitomi Yanaka

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies induced cross-language alignment within individual multilingual LLMs. It does not test whether independently trained models converge with scale, cross-modal convergence, or any other listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The study measures and induces alignment between languages within the same model, not convergence between independent models. Its steering and training deliberately induce alignment, so they do not show that alignment arises without that intervention. Downstream task accuracy results are not rows because they do not directly measure representation similarity; cosine-similarity results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study measures and deliberately induces cross-language alignment inside single multilingual LLMs (Llama3.1-8B, gemma3-4b, Qwen3-4B) via LEACE decomposition and optimal-transport steering/training. It never compares representations between independently trained models, across modalities, across seeds, or across scale, so no version of the convergence claim is tested. 'Discusses' is kept because related work cites the shared-semantic-space literature (Wu et al. 2025).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. Authors conclude CAROT's token-level OT alignment of language-agnostic components, preserving language-specific ones, gives effective alignment targets. Steering improves accuracy by up to 11.2 points without fidelity loss. Training beats prior CLA methods in 11 of 18 settings, but with smaller gains than steering.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes LEACE decomposition and token-level unbalanced optimal transport for within-model cross-language alignment; it does not reproduce a method for testing cross-model convergence.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper selects steering layer and filtering threshold by grid search, but does not report a controlled test of how similarity-measure choices or input choices change the convergence result in the claim.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama3.1-8B, after LEACE erasure, cross-language similarity of parallel sentences exceeds same-language similarity. The erased components are near-identical within a language.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within one multilingual LLM, a linearly separable language component can be removed, leaving content-driven, language-shared representations.

fits_no_version.finding: CAROT steering and CAROT training raise source-target language-agnostic cosine similarity in Llama3.1-8B, peaking near the intervention layer and persisting in later layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicit steering or training can increase cross-language representation similarity within a multilingual LLM.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning causes representation drift: principal angles between pre- and post-training LEACE subspaces average 40.3°, and 32.8° for the covariance subspaces (top 50 eigenvectors).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning substantially rotates the language-related subspaces within one model.

record.problems: The experiments cover only 4–8B parameter models. The reported representation-similarity results are presented in figures without numeric values in the text. Steering and training intentionally induce alignment, so they do not establish spontaneous convergence.
record.rows_left_out: Downstream task accuracy, fidelity, and agreement results were not recorded because they do not directly measure representation similarity. The paper reports them in Sections 6–7 and Tables 1, 3, 7, and 8.

untested.parts: All: no comparison across independently trained models or across scale (only 4–8B models, never compared to each other).
All: no vision models or image-caption pairs.
All: no multiple seeds of one architecture.
All: no mapping or stitching between different models. The cross-language mapping is within one model.
All: no features or circuits compared across models.
All: no cross-model similarity metric or input sensitivity analysis. The OOD-language results concern LEACE erasure, not cross-model convergence.
All: no cross-model alignment measured, so neither its completeness nor its causes are assessed.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is a cross-lingual alignment method paper, off-topic for representation convergence across models. All rows are within-model and either validate the authors' own method or show deliberately induced alignment; none should link to any version. The principal-angle drift result is minor and unrelated to the claim versions, so it is not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: Whether independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data become more aligned as scale and capability increase.
Vision-language alignment for paired images and captions as model performance changes.
Representation convergence across random seeds of the same architecture.
Mapping representations between different models, including with linear maps, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired methods.
Recurrence of shared interpretable features or circuits across models.
Whether measured convergence varies with similarity metric settings or input choice, or disappears out of distribution.
Whether cross-model alignment is incomplete or plateaus, and whether shared data or objectives explain it.

rows.subject: Llama3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compared cosine similarity for intra-language and parallel inter-language sentence pairs across original, remaining, and LEACE-erased representations.
rows.value: figure only; text states inter-language similarity is higher than intra-language similarity
rows.note: This is a comparison of language representations within one model, not alignment across independently trained models.
rows.check: Within-model inter- vs intra-language similarity after the authors' own LEACE decomposition. Not cross-model alignment, and figure-only. Linking to 'none' is correct.

rows.subject: Llama3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Measured intra-language cosine similarity in LEACE-erased sentence representations.
rows.value: figure only; text states intra-language similarity is consistently close to 1
rows.note: This result concerns language-specific components within a single model.
rows.check: This is a validation of the authors' own decomposition method (LEACE-erased components), not a claim measure. It arguably shouldn't be a result row at all.

rows.subject: Llama3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compared source-target cosine similarity of language-agnostic sentence representations before and after CAROT inference-time steering.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between source- and target-language representations
rows.value: figure only; text states similarity increases at the steering layer and remains higher in later layers
rows.note: The alignment is deliberately induced by steering and is within one model across languages.
rows.check: Alignment is induced by the authors' own steering method, within one model. It is an evaluation of their method, not a measurement of convergence arising on its own.

rows.subject: Llama3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Trained with CAROT alignment targets and measured source-target cosine similarity before and after training.

conditions.value: across layers; alignment loss applied at layer 12

rows.measure: Cosine similarity between source- and target-language representations
rows.value: figure only; text states similarity increases most around the training layer and the increase lasts across layers
rows.note: This is an effect of training explicitly to produce aligned representations, within one model.
rows.check: Alignment is induced by training with an explicit alignment loss, within one model. It is the method's own effect, not a claim measure.
